data.name: Gunavan
data.gender_notes: Gunavan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit words ‘gun’ (power, strength) and ‘avan’ (victor). This name symbolizes the power and strength of a victor. In Hindu mythology, it is the name of various deities and legendary figures who have displayed immense power and courage. The name Gunavan carries the meaning “Power, Strength, Victor” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Gunavan usually hope their child will grow to embody power, strength, victor and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embodying the divine power of victory.
data.etymology: Gunavan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Power, Strength, Victor.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gunavan total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Gunavan" signifies a powerful and victorious individual, reflecting the cultural values and traditions that place a high emphasis on strength and success. This name resonates with Indian mythology and folklore, where characters like Lord Rama, Krishna, and Arjuna are revered for their courage, power, and unwavering dedication.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiruitually, "Gunavan" could be interpreted as one who has mastered the three gunas (qualities) of Hinduism - Sattva (purity), Rajas (activity), and Tamas (inertia)- and has thereby achieved victory over material desires and the eternal cycle of birth and rebirth. This name is a reminder that with inner strength and purity, one can triumph over any obstacle.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Gunavan signifies one who possesses virtues or good qualities in abundance. It is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Guna' meaning qualities or virtues, and 'Van' meaning abundance. This name is a reminder to uphold moral values and strive for spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Guna is a title given to several kings and rulers in Hindu history, including King Guna of the Vatsa dynasty during the 6th century BCE.
Another Gunavan was a Chola king who ruled in the late 10th century CE and is known for his patronage of Hindu temples and architecture, including the famous Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur.
